topic: Asking レン out for coffee
title_jp: {日曜|にちよう}、{空いてる|あいてる}？
context: Thursday 3 December: taking {健太|けんた}'s advice, アルちゃん asks レン on LINE to meet for coffee on Sunday in {長野市|ながのし}. レン compares a chain café by the station with an old {喫茶店|きっさてん} near his cinema, and they choose the {喫茶店|きっさてん}.
scene: Thursday night under the kotatsu. You take {健太|けんた}'s advice and ask レン out for coffee. He gives you two places to choose from.

phrases.jp: こっちのほうが{値段|ねだん|price|4}は{高い|たかい}けど、{量|りょう}が{多い|おおい}。
phrases.en: This one is pricier, but you get more.
phrases.note: AのほうがX: the basic way to compare two things.

phrases.jp: {着いたら|ついたら}、{連絡|れんらく}するね。
phrases.en: I'll message you when I get there.
phrases.note: Said before every meet-up in Japan.

phrases.jp: どっちのほうが{人気|にんき}ですか。
phrases.note: Ask staff this when you can't choose between two.

phrases.jp: {雰囲気|ふんいき|atmosphere|4}がいいお{店|みせ}だね。
phrases.en: It's a place with a nice atmosphere.
phrases.note: Cafés, restaurants, even people: {雰囲気|ふんいき}がいい.

phrases.jp: {味|あじ}は{同じ|おなじ}くらいだね。
phrases.note: {同|おな}じくらい = about the same: comparing without a winner.

dialogue_setting: LINE, Thursday evening. アルちゃん writes first; レン, as usual, takes a while to reply.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: レンさん、こんばんは！{急|きゅう|sudden|4}だけど、{今度|こんど}の{日曜|にちよう}、{空いてる|あいてる|to be free (time)|4}？
dialogue.en: Evening, レン! This is sudden, but are you free this Sunday?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: よかったら、{長野|ながの}でコーヒーでもどうかな…
dialogue.en: If you like, maybe a coffee in {長野|ながの}…?

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: {遅く|おそく}なってごめん。{日曜|にちよう}は{予定|よてい|plans|4}ないよ。うれしい
dialogue.en: Sorry for the slow reply. I've got no plans on Sunday. I'm happy you asked.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: {駅前|えきまえ}の{チェーン店|チェーンてん|chain store|3}と、{映画館|えいがかん}の{近く|ちかく}の{喫茶店|きっさてん|old-style coffee shop|3}、どっちがいい？
dialogue.en: A chain café by the station, or a coffee shop near the cinema: which do you prefer?

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: {喫茶店|きっさてん|old-style coffee shop|3}は{チェーン店|チェーンてん|chain store|3}に{比べて|くらべて}ちょっと{高い|たかい}けど、{雰囲気|ふんいき|atmosphere|4}がいいよ
dialogue.en: The coffee shop is a bit pricier than the chain, but it has a nice atmosphere.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: {マスター||owner (of a café or bar)|3}が{自分|じぶん}で{豆|まめ|(coffee) beans|3}を{焙煎|ばいせん|roasting (coffee)|1}してるんだ
dialogue.en: The owner roasts the beans himself.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: じゃあ{喫茶店|きっさてん|old-style coffee shop|3}がいい！{駅|えき}に{着いたら|ついたら}{連絡|れんらく}するね
dialogue.en: Then the coffee shop! I'll message you when I get to the station.

dialogue.speaker: レン
dialogue.jp: うん、2{時|じ}に。{雪|ゆき}が{降ったら|ふったら}、{無理|むり}しないでね
dialogue.en: OK, at 2. If it snows, don't push yourself.

listening.intro: Earlier that evening, an announcement at the supermarket just before closing.
listening.title: スーパーのお{知らせ|しらせ}
listening.place: The shopping-street supermarket, {鷹ノ原|たかのはら}

lines.jp: ご{来店|らいてん|coming to the shop|2}ありがとうございます。{当店|とうてん|this shop|2}は{夜|よる}8{時|じ}で{閉店|へいてん|closing (a shop)|3}いたします。
lines.en: Thank you for shopping with us. The shop closes at 8 p.m.

lines.jp: ただいま、お{弁当|べんとう}とお{惣菜|そうざい|ready-made side dishes|3}が{半額|はんがく|half price|3}です。
lines.en: Right now, boxed meals and ready-made dishes are half price.

listening.question: お{店|みせ}は{何時|なんじ}に{閉まります|しまります}か。
listening.explain: {夜|よる}8{時|じ}で{閉店|へいてん}: the shop closes at 8 p.m.

grammar.form: verbs: た-form + ら ({着|つ}いた → {着|つ}いたら, {降|ふ}った → {降|ふ}ったら) · い-adj: -かったら ({高|たか}い → {高|たか}かったら) · noun / な-adj: + だったら ({雨|あめ}だったら, {暇|ひま}だったら)
grammar.explanation: Two uses: 'if' ({雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}ったら, it may or may not happen) and 'when / once' ({着|つ}いたら, it will happen, then the next step). The second half can be a request, plan or offer, which と can't do. Build it from the た-form: {着|つ}いたら, not {着|つ}くたら.

examples.jp: {仕事|しごと}が{終わったら|おわったら}、{電話|でんわ}するね。
examples.en: I'll call you when I finish work.

examples.jp: もっと{安かったら|やすかったら}、{買う|かう}んだけど。
examples.en: If it were cheaper, I'd buy it.

quiz.question: {家|いえ}に＿＿、すぐお{風呂|ふろ}に{入りたい|はいりたい}。
quiz.en: As soon as I get home, I want to get in the bath.
quiz.explain: た-form + ら: {帰|かえ}った → {帰|かえ}ったら.

quiz_more.question: もし{明日|あした}＿＿、また{今度|こんど}にしよう。
quiz_more.en: If it's rain tomorrow, let's do it another time.
quiz_more.explain: Nouns take だったら: {雨|あめ}だったら.

quiz_more.question: その{店|みせ}、そんなに＿＿{行かない|いかない}よ。
quiz_more.en: If that place is so expensive, I'm not going.
quiz_more.explain: い-adjectives: drop い, add かったら.

kanji.where: On the wooden sign of the {喫茶店|きっさてん}, in the photo レン sends you later that night.
kanji.breakdown: {自家焙煎|じかばいせん}: 自家 one's own house + 焙煎 roasting → beans roasted by the shop itself.
kanji.related: {自家製|じかせい} = homemade (bread, jam, sauces): another word you'll see on menus.

tip.title: A {喫茶店|きっさてん} is not just a café
tip.body: A {喫茶店|きっさてん} is an old-style coffee house with a マスター behind the counter, ナポリタン and thick toast. カフェ sounds newer and lighter. Many {喫茶店|きっさてん} do a モーニング set before 11: coffee with free toast and an egg.

challenge.prompt: レン: 「{駅|えき}のどこで{待ち合わせ|まちあわせ|meeting up|4}する？」 Tell him you'll send a LINE once you get off the train.
challenge.model_answer: {電車|でんしゃ}を{降りたら|おりたら}、LINEするね。
challenge.explanation: {降|お}りたら comes from the た-form {降|お}りた + ら: 'once I've got off'. The first step happens, then the second (LINEする). Plain form + ね suits a friendly chat with レン.
challenge.hint: た-form + ら, then what you'll do

vocab.note: {急|きゅう}だけど / {急|きゅう}にごめん: softens a last-minute ask.
{空|あ}いてる？ = are you free? Also seats: {席|せき}が{空|あ}いてる.
{予定|よてい}がある = I've got plans (a polite way to say no).
Opposite: {個人店|こじんてん}, an independent shop.
{喫|きっ} drink + {茶|さ} tea + {店|てん} shop. See today's tip.
Careful: it's ふんいき, though many young people say ふいんき.
What regulars call the man behind the counter. A woman owner: ママ.
Coffee beans, soy beans. {豆腐|とうふ} = tofu.
{値段|ねだん}が{高|たか}い / {安|やす}い. On tags you'll see {価格|かかく}.

kanji_study.parts: 亻 person radical + 直 straight → what a person says straight out when you ask: the price, the value.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 植 (plant): 植 has 木 tree on the left, 値 has 亻 person.

kanji_study.parts: 宀 roof radical + 正 correct → putting each thing in its right place under the roof: fixed, settled.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 完 (complete): both have 宀, but 完 has 元 underneath, 定 has a shape like 正.

extras.title: Comparing when you shop
extras.title_jp: お{店|みせ}で{比べる|くらべる}
extras.intro: Useful lines when you can't decide.

items.jp: こちらとこちらは、どう{違います|ちがいます}か。
items.en: What's the difference between this one and this one?
items.note: Point at both. Polite and very common.

items.jp: もう{少し|すこし}{安い|やすい}のはありますか。
items.en: Do you have anything a bit cheaper?

items.jp: {一番|いちばん}{人気|にんき}なのはどれですか。
items.note: Staff love this question in restaurants.

extras.title: The classic {喫茶店|きっさてん} menu
extras.title_jp: {喫茶店|きっさてん|old-style coffee shop|3}のメニュー
extras.intro: What you'll find in an old coffee house.

items.note: The default order: ブレンドひとつ.
Bright green, very retro, very photogenic.
Coffee price + free toast and egg, mornings only.
